races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Belfast Live: Number 1 For News And Sport Handicap

runners_data.name: Teologia
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here and likely to dictate from the off; her recent win came at 10f on good ground and she steps up to 10.5f on soft for the first time, which is a stamina query, though her prominent style is ideally suited to this race shape; cheekpieces noted, 22 days since last run.

runners_data.name: Hassaniya
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has placed twice at 8f on good and heavy ground but has yet to win; steps up sharply in trip to 10.5f here and the soft ground is a potential ally for stamina; 31 days off, handler O'Callaghan has 2 from 14 in the last fortnight suggesting modest yard form.

runners_data.name: Dreoilin
runners_data.note: Has placed twice on soft going including a second over 10f, suggesting this trip and ground combination is genuinely within her compass; prominent style means she should travel in a good position behind Teologia, though Bolger's yard is running at a modest 1-from-8 in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Aquilla Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has been off 236 days — the significant layoff is the primary concern; placed over 7f on heavy ground which shows soft-surface ability, but jumping up to 10.5f first time out after a lengthy absence with a 5lb claimer is a stack of unknowns.

runners_data.name: Espritroyale
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but has only one run in five on similar ground in her recent history, making the soft going a genuine question mark; all five recent runs have been at shorter trips (6-10f on good) and the step up here lacks a comparable form line to lean on.

runners_data.name: Roaming Coyote
runners_data.note: Ran second over 10f on good ground 19 days ago which is the most relevant recent form in the race; prominent style means he should land a useful position and his four soft-ground runs all produced similar finishing positions, suggesting consistency rather than a soft-ground flyer.

runners_data.name: The Holy Apostle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose most recent run was just 10 days ago, and his form string of 3-7-5-0-0 in varying conditions suggests he is better fresh than after recent hard races; yet to show he stays beyond 8f and the step to 10.5f is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Chapel Island
runners_data.note: Trainer A Oliver, 23 days since last run; a genuine hold-up horse by nature whose tendency to fade in the finish is a concern on soft ground — pushed into a midfield map position here because there are too many rear-of-field types for all to sit where they want, which further compromises his chance.

runners_data.name: Connecteo
runners_data.note: Has form figures of 2/12f which is the one glimmer of staying-trip ability, though he has otherwise been well beaten and fades; his natural inclination to race from behind is squeezed by the overcrowded hold-up section of this field, meaning he is unlikely to travel where he wants, which undermines an already modest profile.

runners_data.name: Arizona Star
runners_data.note: Placed at 10f on heavy ground which is his one piece of soft-surface credibility; all four recent runs have been well back in the field and the STYLE_FIT flag — combined with being displaced from his natural rear position — means the race is unlikely to unfold in a way that showcases whatever ability he has.

runners_data.name: Amrum
runners_data.note: The most interesting hold-up horse in the race: a winner over 10f on good ground 19 days ago, and two of her five runs have come on soft or heavy; her natural style is to come from off the pace and she has demonstrated she can finish out a strong gallop, making her the most credible threat from the back group.

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground and has the most soft-ground experience of the prominent group (10 runs from 13 on similar); prominent style suits perfectly in a race Teologia is likely to set up from the front, and the Harrington yard has five from 29 in the past fortnight — quiet but not dormant.

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature but pushed into midfield on the map because the field's rear is oversubscribed; his form figures of 0-0-0-6-7 are largely uninspiring and on soft ground at an extended trip, being compromised in positioning makes a big performance difficult to construct.

races.paceDynamic: Teologia is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious rival likely to push her from the outset, she should be able to control tempo from the front on soft ground over 1m2½f at Down Royal. Behind her, Hassaniya, Dreoilin, Roaming Coyote and Glamazon are all prominent types who will be competing for the positions immediately behind the leader, meaning the early order will be busier than it looks on paper. The field contains more hold-up and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Chapel Island, Connecteo, Arizona Star and Captain Con are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because they are unlikely to secure their natural rear-of-field berths in this congested middle section. On soft ground at this trip, with Teologia setting a steady, uncontested tempo, the race shape strongly favours horses who travel prominently and have the stamina to sustain their effort through the testing final stages — hold-up horses dependent on a strong gallop to set up a late run are at a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.title: Teologia Controls, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Teologia dictates a modest uncontested pace and the soft ground ensures stamina is the key factor from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If Teologia dictates a modest uncontested pace and the soft ground ensures stamina is the key factor from the home turn.

scenarios.body: If Teologia goes too slow and triggers a sprint-finish that allows a stayer grinding from midfield to pick off tired rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Increase Blows Field Apart
scenarios.trigger: If the large prominent contingent pushes the early gallop faster than expected and the soft ground turns the race into an attrition test.
scenarios.body: If the large prominent contingent pushes the early gallop faster than expected and the soft ground turns the race into an attrition test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Mover Lands Different Shape
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected tactical development — wide draw, early incident, or late market confidence — reshapes the race and an unconsidered type runs a career-best.
scenarios.body: If an unexpected tactical development — wide draw, early incident, or late market confidence — reshapes the race and an unconsidered type runs a career-best.

watchPoints.text: Amrum is the primary danger — if the pace is anything other than truly steady, her combination of a recent win, soft-ground form and ability to sustain a finish from midfield makes her the most likely horse to ambush the prominent leaders in the straight.

The prominent group of Hassaniya, Dreoilin and Roaming Coyote will all be jostling for the same positions behind Teologia in the opening stages; any crowding or checked momentum in the first quarter-mile could compromise the outcome for multiple market fancies simultaneously.

Aquilla Star's 236-day absence is a serious flag — horses returning from that long a break at a new and longer trip on soft ground can either show improved freshness or simply not be ready; watch the market move closely for a guide.

Chapel Island and Connecteo are both trained by A Oliver and both are genuine hold-up horses squeezed into midfield; if either manages to find a cleaner run than their map position suggests, they could be bigger-priced contributors to a place, but their finishing tendencies on soft ground limit upside.

Soft going is consistent across the entire Down Royal card today and will only ease as the day progresses — any horse whose stamina profile is borderline for 10.5f on good ground should be treated with caution on today's surface.

races.name: Mongey Communications Handicap

runners_data.name: Slaney Swagger
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has placed twice at a mile from the front end on good ground but has not run for 192 days — the fitness query is significant and soft going is a fresh ask; hg:p headgear retained but the layoff is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Cleopatra's Needle
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with genuine each-way form at this sort of trip, including a win at 1m6f on good, and the booking of Chris Hayes is a positive; last seen 69 days ago but that is not prohibitive, though all five recent runs have been on good ground and soft is untested.

runners_data.name: Folk Warrior
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose natural finishing style has been compromised by the field's composition and mapped to midfield — history shows five of seven starts on similar going yet no places, and the fade-in-finish flag reinforces a pattern of not delivering; discount accordingly.

runners_data.name: Simpson's Paradox
runners_data.note: Genuine closer who has been absorbed into midfield mapping because of the hold-up glut — recent form reads 8/20/7 positions and a soft-ground run was unplaced, so the style mismatch and consistency issues combine to limit appeal here.

runners_data.name: Albatala
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old stayer with place form at 1m7f and 2m1f on good, and trainer McConnell landed one in the T14 window; the redistribution means he races out of his natural hold-up role, but his proven stamina at extreme trips gives some insurance if the ground gets genuinely testing.

runners_data.name: Copper Craft
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who flags fade-in-finish across his recent runs and whose single soft-ground start produced a last-of-nine; mapped to midfield as a redistributed hold-up type, the fade flag and going concern compound the style disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Hosanna Power
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in the 7-13 range, no wins and no places in recent starts, and the redistribution away from true hold-up position further reduces any chance this handicap debutant has of exploiting an exposed mark.

runners_data.name: Maker's Mark
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a 9-9-9-9 run sequence, fade-in-finish flag, and only one qualifying soft-ground start; with an apprentice claimer taking off 7lbs the weight is manageable but the form profile offers no encouragement.

runners_data.name: Coul Dore
runners_data.note: Crawford three-year-old who was placed at 1m2f on good and has soft-ground form (2/5 qualifying runs) — the fade flag appears but this is the right trip and Leigh Roche is an experienced pilot; worth noting as an each-way outsider if the race cuts up for stamina.

runners_data.name: Stonyfalls
runners_data.note: Ran only yesterday (1 day since last run) which is an enormous concern regardless of style; a natural hold-up horse redistributed to midfield, already flagged as fading in finishes, and operating at 7f up to now — the combination of fatigue, trip, and style mismatch makes this a very difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Swift Charm
runners_data.note: Three-year-old stayer who has placed twice at 1m2f on good ground for Crawford, hold-up style with a fade flag but distance form is encouraging; soft ground is a fresh test but of the lower-rated closers she has the most relevant recent form.

runners_data.name: Thistle Cross
runners_data.note: Young three-year-old with a 0-0-0-0 recent record and no form beyond 8f, mapped to midfield as a redistributed closer who has never placed in four starts; style disadvantage and an absence of soft-ground or trip form make this a very difficult runner to support.

runners_data.name: Onyeisi
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR=56 among the hold-up group, with a place at 1m2f on Stansted recently and decent form at 1m2f on good; Robbie Colgan is a capable jockey and the consistency of the form string (2-2-4-7-10) gives the best profile among the mid-rear group.

runners_data.name: Talking Tough
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran flagged as fading in finishes, redistribution to midfield from his natural hold-up position, and soft-ground form of 11/15 speaks for itself; the class has been clearly exposed and this looks a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Kilgharrahs Love
runners_data.note: Four-year-old without a jockey listed at time of analysis, mapped to midfield as a redistributed hold-up type — has one career place and soft-going experience was unplaced; hard to construct a winning argument without riding arrangements confirmed.

runners_data.name: Marians Gal
runners_data.note: Prominent-style six-year-old trained by Kevin Michael Smith who has been firing shots (2nd, 3rd, 4th at 1m2-1m3f on standard) and whose trainer has been 2/4 in the T14 window; genuine hold-up-adjacent style fits tracking Rising Sky and this looks one of the more interesting handicap angles at a realistic price.

runners_data.name: Rising Sky
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner at OR=60 and confirmed front-runner under Sam Coen who will lead from flag-fall — soft ground is his main query (2/15 qualifying runs) and the STYLE_FIT flag notes he is technically racing out of role at this trip for this course, but as the sole pace-setter he has complete control of the tempo and that is a significant tactical weapon.

races.paceDynamic: Rising Sky is the sole confirmed front-runner and, at OR=60 the top-rated runner in the field, will stride to the front from the off and set a sustainable, controlled tempo on soft ground over 1m2½f — there is no rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, meaning he dictates entirely on his own terms. Cleopatra's Needle and Marians Gal will track in prominent positions just off the leader, giving the race a tidy shape with a small group up front and the bulk of the field strung out behind. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the track can absorb: Stonyfalls, Thistle Cross, Folk Warrior, Talking Tough, Kilgharrahs Love and others have been redistributed to midfield on the map but are genuine closers who will find themselves further back than ideal, diluting their effectiveness. With one uncontested front-runner setting a soft-ground tempo he can manage, this race shape strongly favours horses that can sit prominent or just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — pure hold-up horses face the dual disadvantage of soft ground and a pace that may never be truly testing enough to set up a late surge.

scenarios.body: If Rising Sky bowls along unchallenged and the soft ground does not fully negate his stamina reserves at this trip.

scenarios.body: If Rising Sky's soft-ground stamina runs out inside the final furlong and one of the prominent trackers swoops.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground and steady pace creates a stamina test severe enough to string the field out and allow a late-running stayer to pick through.
scenarios.body: If the soft ground and steady pace creates a stamina test severe enough to string the field out and allow a late-running stayer to pick through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Unable To Land
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is too moderate on soft ground and the true hold-up horses — Stonyfalls, Folk Warrior, Thistle Cross — cannot bridge the gap from their rearward positions.
scenarios.body: If the pace is too moderate on soft ground and the true hold-up horses — Stonyfalls, Folk Warrior, Thistle Cross — cannot bridge the gap from their rearward positions.

watchPoints.text: Rising Sky has soft-ground form of only 2/15 qualifying runs — if he struggles in the ground and stops quickly in the straight, the entire front-end scenario collapses and the race becomes a scramble for Cleopatra's Needle and Marians Gal to pick up the pieces.

Stonyfalls ran only yesterday and even if the trainer declares him fit, a horse racing for the second consecutive day on soft ground in a 17-runner handicap is a major red flag — monitor market to see if connections believe he is viable.

The field contains at least eight runners with a fade-in-finish pattern (Folk Warrior, Copper Craft, Maker's Mark, Coul Dore, Stonyfalls, Swift Charm, Thistle Cross, Talking Tough) — if the pace is slow, these horses cannot manufacture a finish even if they get into the right position.
Kilgharrahs Love has no jockey recorded — confirm riding arrangements at declaration stage as an unknown apprentice or late booking could materially affect the market and running plan.

Marians Gal's trainer Kevin Michael Smith has gone 2/4 in the 14-day window and the horse has placed in three of its last four starts at this trip — watch for market support as a prominent player who benefits most if Rising Sky weakens.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Irish EBF Ulster Oaks Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Fiver Friday
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a win and place at this course on good ground under Carroll for Cromwell; steps into a front-running role that suits her style, though soft ground is a question given her best form is on quicker surfaces — she's done it on similar before but a clean lead here is her biggest asset.

runners_data.name: Apercu
runners_data.note: Consistent campaigner but recent form on good ground shows she's struggled to land a blow in this grade; blinkers on, and while she handles this trip, a string of mid-division finishes on good suggests she needs more pace than Fiver Friday is likely to generate today.

runners_data.name: Lady Lilac
runners_data.note: Murphy's four-year-old steps up from sprint trips to 1m2½f for the first time in a while; her best form is on good or faster, and the move to soft on a longer trip looks a risk — Sam Coen's 5lb claim helps the weight but the going and distance combination is untested territory.

runners_data.name: Narlita
runners_data.note: Veteran seven-year-old whose record on soft is solid, including a win at 12f on heavy ground — the going is genuinely in her favour — but she is a natural front-runner who the map has pushed to midfield because of the congested pace picture; her race hinges on whether she can creep closer than her mapped position suggests.

runners_data.name: Beauparc
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on standard and has placed on soft at this distance, so trip and surface are suitable; Gerard Keane's six-year-old is wearing a tongue tie and naturally wants to race prominently, but with so many pace types in this field she'll likely find herself racing more patiently than ideal.

runners_data.name: Thrifty Of Digby
runners_data.note: Harrington's five-year-old has won twice at 10f on good ground and showed respectable soft-ground form in a Listed race; she's a natural forwardly-positioned type who couldn't get that position and is shown in midfield, though if she can slot in close enough to Fiver Friday she has the soft-ground ability to threaten.

runners_data.name: Chica Guerrera
runners_data.note: Mark Fahey's four-year-old has placed on soft at 10f and this is a slight step up in trip; she naturally wants to race prominently and at 127lbs is near the bottom of the weights — Whelan is a positive booking — but the midfield map position means her finishing effort depends on not being bottled up in the straight.

runners_data.name: Chablis Rock
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old won at Leopardstown over 12f on good ground last time and placed at The Curragh — unexposed at this distance and rated 90, making her one of the most interesting form angles in the field; McDonogh takes the ride and her limited soft-ground exposure (tongue tie noted) is the only uncertainty around a horse who looks ahead of her mark.

runners_data.name: Enchanted Lady
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type, the only one mapped to that position on merit; her form is limited — three runs, best is a fourth — and she has no soft-ground evidence to speak of, so while she is in the right tactical position for a truly strong pace she lacks the raw ability to capitalise.

runners_data.name: Diamond Exchange
runners_data.note: Won twice on good-to-soft and soft conditions, so the going suits well; Harrington's four-year-old is a front-runner at heart who is carrying a tongue tie and pads, and being pushed into a midfield role by the crowded pace scenario is a real concern — her best runs come when she can dictate or sit handy.

runners_data.name: Stars Will Shine
runners_data.note: Meade's three-year-old won over 7f on good and has placed at 8f — today's step up to 1m2½f on soft is a significant ask; Chris Hayes takes over and the yard is in decent form, but the distance and surface combination represents a leap into the unknown and she may not truly see out the trip.

runners_data.name: Liberation Date
runners_data.note: Foley's three-year-old won over 7f on standard and has placed twice at that trip; she is fundamentally a prominent type shifted to the rear by the map because the field is light on genuine hold-up horses — her chance is compromised by racing against her natural style, and the step to 1m2½f on soft is another hurdle.

races.paceDynamic: Fiver Friday is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure expected, Gary Carroll can dictate an honest but manageable gallop on soft ground over 1m2½f — a distance that suits patient, sustained finishing rather than a sprint finish. Behind her, a cluster of natural prominent racers — Narlita, Beauparc, Thrifty Of Digby, Chica Guerrera, Diamond Exchange and Liberation Date — cannot all secure their preferred position and several will be forced to race further back than ideal, compressing the midfield and blurring the pace picture. Fiver Friday therefore sets the tempo essentially unchallenged, which on soft ground at this trip tends to reward horses who travel smoothly in her wake and finish with purpose rather than those who need a truly burning gallop to make their move count. This race shape — a single, uncontested leader on a testing surface — most favours the prominent-to-midfield tracker who can sit a length or two off the pace, conserve energy in the soft ground, and produce a clean, sustained finish over the final two furlongs; genuine hold-up horses and those pushed far back against their nature face the sternest task.

watchPoints.text: Chablis Rock is the form danger — OR 90, three-year-old, unexposed at 1m2½f, won last time at Leopardstown, and McDonogh in the saddle; if she handles the soft she is the most likely horse to peg back Fiver Friday.

Monitor the early positions closely: Narlita, Beauparc, Diamond Exchange, Thrifty Of Digby and Chica Guerrera all want to be prominent but cannot all get there — any crowding or checking in the first two furlongs could compromise several runners simultaneously.

Fiver Friday's soft-ground record is worth watching — her best form is on good or good-to-firm, and if the soft ground blunts her more than expected she could be vulnerable in the final furlong having set the pace alone.

Stars Will Shine is stepping up sharply in trip from 8f to 1m2½f on soft — watch how she travels at halfway, as this is the key test of whether Meade's filly stays the distance or cries enough entering the straight.

Liberation Date's jockey Orla Tynan (7lb claimer) is riding out of role on a horse mapped to hold-up but naturally preferring to race prominently — how she manages the early stages will determine whether Liberation Date is involved at all in the finish.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Ulster Derby (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: New Zealand
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner under Jack Cleary for Aidan O'Brien; steps up markedly in trip to 1m5f having shown stamina over 13f at Goodwood, soft ground not a concern, and uncontested lead here is a major tactical asset though OR 101 is a career high.

runners_data.name: Shosholoza
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien in strong 14-day form (9/61); has placed on soft going and won at 9f on Heathfield, making this step to 1m5f a query, but prominent style suits the race shape and he drops significantly in class from Group company.

runners_data.name: Trojan Fighter
runners_data.note: Willie Lee-ridden for Pat Twomey; has a win over 13f at Goodwood in good ground and placed four times in similar conditions, making this trip his optimum — prominent style ideally placed to track New Zealand and challenge late.

runners_data.name: Harmani
runners_data.note: G M Lyons yard lightly represented; has soft-ground form (placed at 8f and 7f on soft), but his natural front-running instincts will be compromised here — the prominent slots are full, and he is expected to be held in an uncharacteristic midfield position throughout.

runners_data.name: Huff'n'puff
runners_data.note: De Bromhead in decent 14-day form; recent winner at 10f, soft ground no concern, and runs prominently — sits fourth in the betting logic and well-positioned to attack New Zealand if it weakens in the straight.

runners_data.name: Mergus Serrator
runners_data.note: Style unknown; three runs all in good ground, no soft-going form to assess, and the step to 1m5f is uncharted — Gary Carroll is experienced but this represents a significant leap into the unknown for Gavin Cromwell's charge.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Stars
runners_data.note: Weld, who has had only six runners in 14 days; won over 12f at Salisbury and naturally wants to race up with the pace — however, the front positions are occupied, and he is likely to find himself racing wide of his comfort zone in a midfield berth, reducing his chance markedly.

runners_data.name: Madbadanddangerous
runners_data.note: Noel Meade runner with soft-ground win (1/7f on soft) and four placings on soft across five runs; naturally a prominent type but bumped to the rear by the congestion up front — Gavin Ryan will need luck from an unfamiliar position.

runners_data.name: Wyman
runners_data.note: Harrington yard in reasonable form; the most genuine hold-up runner in the field and placed on soft going over 10f, but a 66-day absence is a significant concern and the tempo must collapse for this profile to succeed.

runners_data.name: Pierre Grosse
runners_data.note: Fellow Harrington runner, style uncertain, placed on good ground at up to 10f; apprentice Keithen Kennedy takes 5lb, and the step to soft going at 1m5f on a 15-day turnaround is unexplored territory — no obvious tactical edge here.

races.paceDynamic: New Zealand is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead under Jack Cleary, should be allowed to dictate an uncontested, measured gallop on soft ground over 1m5f — a test that will stretch the field physically from an early stage. Shosholoza, Trojan Fighter, and Huff'n'puff are all natural prominent types who will settle just off New Zealand, creating a compact early order but not a pressured one, meaning the tempo is likely to be honest rather than brutal on this ground. Harmani and Bay Of Stars are both genuine front-runners by nature but have been redistributed to midfield in this map because the prominent berths are already claimed; they are unlikely to secure their natural position and will find themselves in unfamiliar territory, softening their chances. This race shape — an uncontested, sustainable pace on soft ground over a staying trip — strongly favours horses that travel prominently, finish stoutly, and have soft-ground form, with genuine hold-up horses carrying the least tactical advantage as the gallop is unlikely to be strong enough to produce a true late-swoop finish.

watchPoints.text: New Zealand's response to being sent to the front in this company is the pivotal factor — if Jack Cleary can control the tempo on the soft ground, this horse's chance is maximised; if he bowls along too freely early, the race is blown open.

Harmani and Bay Of Stars are both natural front-runners who will almost certainly be denied their preferred prominent position — watch how their jockeys manage the first two furlongs, as any energy wasted scrubbing along or fighting for position could compromise their entire race.

Wyman has been off 66 days for a yard that has had runners in the interim — check for any fitness indicators in the paddock, as a hold-up horse returning off a break on soft ground needs to be cherry-ripe.

The going report confirms soft throughout the entire card at Down Royal — all seven races on soft means the ground is consistently testing, and horses with proven soft-ground form (Harmani, Madbadanddangerous, Wyman) carry a meaningful surface edge over rivals whose form is entirely on good or good-to-firm.

Trojan Fighter is the only runner who has won over this exact trip (13f Goodwood) in a form line that also includes a soft-ground entry — if New Zealand weakens, his stamina and proximity to the pace make him the obvious beneficiary.

races.paceDynamic: Grey Fable is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner handicap and, with Deluca Chop and Jurality as the natural prominent types, the pace is sustainable rather than searching — Grey Fable can dictate from the front on soft ground at Down Royal without being seriously pressured into overdoing it. Folly Beach and Just Another Eagle may try to track closely, but none of the other prominent-placed horses in the map have the profile to seriously challenge Grey Fable for the lead in the early stages, meaning the fractions are likely to be measured and the race run at a tempo that suits those who can travel within striking distance. The field is significantly loaded with hold-up types — Pebble Island, Numidia, Patrick Street, Calmafterthestorm, Plus Or Minus, Idomything, and Milverton are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield in the map simply because there are too many deep closers and nowhere near enough pace to accommodate them all at the rear cleanly. This race shape, with one uncontested leader setting an honest but not brutal tempo on soft ground over 1m5f, strongly favours prominent and early-prominent racers who can save ground, travel into the race naturally, and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out — genuine hold-up horses face a return-to-form task against the clock here.

races.paceDynamic: Steel Cut is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be allowed to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop on soft ground over 1m5f — a setup that typically suits a horse capable of conserving energy in front rather than burning it off in a pace duel. Murat and Daddy Long Legs are the most credible prominent types to track Steel Cut, while Duvessa can also race forwardly from her likely draw position. This field contains more pace than the map can accommodate: Joe Cool and Double Indian are genuine prominent and hold-up types respectively who are likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield given how many horses want to race prominently, meaning their natural tactical advantage is diluted. The race shape — a lone front-runner setting a measured soft-ground gallop with two or three trackers — strongly favours a prominent racer who can sit within a length or two of Steel Cut, conserve energy through the middle portion, and finish off on softening ground; a horse who has to cover ground from midfield or further back faces a stiff ask given the likely lack of a truly searching gallop to bring them into it.
